question: When performing a biopsy of a suspected malignant bone tumour, the incision should be transverse so that it can be excised with a wide ellipse during subsequent definitive surgery.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. The statement is FALSE. Biopsy incisions must always be longitudinal, placed in line with the future resection, to avoid contaminating adjacent compartments. A transverse wound is a serious surgical error in bone tumour biopsy.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — that statement is FALSE. Biopsy incisions must be LONGITUDINAL and placed along the planned resection line. A transverse incision crosses multiple tissue compartments, contaminating them all, which can render limb salvage impossible and may force amputation.
